Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:37: And the Righteous One [Tzaddik/Yesod] is called "faithful" [ne'eman] - for he explained in the Tikkunim (page 34b) and the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 229a) that in the Righteous One is the secret of "AMeN," which equals 91 in numerical value, like YaHDoNHY [the combined spelling of YHVH and Adonai], and in the Righteous One is this Name, for he is called "all" [kol], in heaven and earth, holding fast in heaven and earth, as they explained in the Tikkunim (page 29a); and in "Amen" he explained, at the end of Parashat Vayelech (page 285b), that it is an acronym for "El Melech Ne'eman" [God, faithful King] - behold, "faithful" is in the Righteous One. It follows that wherever "Amen" is found, as explained in Parashat Vayelech - see there - "faithful" is found. And further, they explained in Tractate Shabbat (page 104a) concerning the [final] nun: "a bent nun, a straight nun" [alluding to a faithful (ne'eman) bent, a faithful (ne'eman) upright].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:38: It follows, in general, that in all four letters of the Name "faithful" is found, and this is the essence of faith - and therefore the word "emunah," first found in the Torah, is found with the Name YHVH, as he says (Genesis 15:6), "and he believed in YHVH," and so too afterward again (Exodus 14:31), "and they believed in YHVH." And you already know what Rashbi, peace be upon him, said (Tikkunei Zohar, page 92b), that in this Name is the essence of Israel's faith - and we copied his words in the Gate of Fear, chapter 1 - where he said: and therefore the faith of Israel is set in these four letters, in all their appellations they set names for this Name. And he explained there that the Cause of causes unifies the four letters YHVH - it follows that the faithful one is bound to His great Name and to the Cause of causes - happy is he.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:39: And behold, concerning the matter of joy, we have already explained that from trust and faith joy comes - for the servant who trusts in his master and believes he will repay him the reward of his service manifold, will serve with joy, and he is joyful in whatever is decreed upon him, and so he endures everything, like a sick man who eats bitter medicines for the sake of healing - and the one who endures is free from the worries of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:40: Further, there is benefit in joy, as in the story (Ta'anit 22a) of the two men of whom Elijah said that they were destined for the World to Come, because they were men who brought joy - when they saw a sad man, they would cheer him, and when they saw two people quarreling with one another, they would speak jesting words to them until they made peace between them. And so too concerning halachah, one first speaks words of jest, to open the heart to study with joy (Shabbat 30b) - but not the joy of scoffers or the joy of the stingy, but rather a matter of a commandment that gladdens the heart, as it is written (Psalms 19:9), "the precepts of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart" - and all this is the joy of a commandment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:41: Upon the attribute of joy depends the positive commandment that one justify His judgment concerning all that befalls him, as it is said (Deuteronomy 8:5), "and you shall know in your heart, that as a man chastens his son, so the LORD your God chastens you." And if, after a person has repented, his affairs do not improve as before, then it is a positive commandment that he consider in his heart that his affairs turned to evil for his own good - for before he repented, the Holy One, blessed be He, was paying the reward of a commandment in order to expel him from the World to Come. And all this depends on the attribute of joy - one who is joyful in his portion, which God, blessed be He, apportioned to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:42: But the way for a person to rejoice in his portion is that he rejoice over the evil just as over the good, and endure it with joy - for the one who endures is free from the worries of the world, for the one who endures makes do with the little he has, saying, it is enough for me what the Creator, blessed be He, decrees for me.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:43: And now look and see that joy encompasses everything - for whoever worries over this world has no rest all his days, for he is always thinking of earning money, and does not content himself with what God, blessed be He, has apportioned to him; and therefore whoever rejoices in his portion is rich, even if he is poor, for he rejoices in the Name, for He is his inheritance - as it is written (Lamentations 3:24), "the LORD is my portion, says my soul," and it is written (Psalms 16:5), "the LORD is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup," and so on, and it is said (ibid. 105:3), "let the heart of those who seek the LORD rejoice." And this attribute is only in the souls of the righteous, who are in complete pleasantness in the matter of their service and in great joy in separation, as it is said (ibid. 32:11), "be glad in the LORD and rejoice, O righteous, and shout for joy, all you upright in heart," and it is said (ibid. 97:11), "light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:44: Therefore let every person place his joy upon the Torah, and at the time he performs the commandments let him rejoice in his heart that he has merited to be a servant of the supernal King, before whom the sons of the heights bow - and so David said (ibid. 119:162), "I rejoice at Your word, as one who finds great spoil" - and whoever performs a commandment with joy has a thousand times the reward of one who is merely commanded.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:45: Abraham and David were occupied with Torah all day, glorifying and praising with songs and praises of the Holy One, blessed be He, raising their voice in joy - and then all their limbs were saved in their pleasant goodness, and the holy spirit was sent within them, and their heart rejoiced and was filled with love of the Holy One, blessed be He, and their soul was bound in gladness, and secrets and novel insights of the higher realm were revealed to them - because they feared the Name, and pleasantness entered their upright heart. And this is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Song of Songs 5:6), "my soul departed at his word," and (Proverbs 23:16), "and my kidneys shall exult when your lips speak upright things." And so David said (Psalms 104:1), "bless the LORD, O my soul" - because the soul ascends upward, and just as it knows the matter of its secret, so it will love the Creator and treasure His commandments; and when the soul reaches its excellent place, to which it is similar, it will then unify Him in His hidden depths and delight in His chambers, and at every time and moment desire His love, and remember Him at night upon its couch - then the Name, blessed be He, sends into it the desire of joy, along the lines of what is said (Isaiah 61:10), "I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul shall be joyful in my God" - and happy is the soul that merits to see that joy. And the Shechinah rests only from within joy, and all the prophets did not prophesy whenever they wished, but rather directed their minds and sat joyful and of good heart and secluded themselves - for prophecy rests neither from within sadness nor from within laziness, but from within joy; therefore the sons of the prophets had before them a tambourine, a flute, and a lyre, and sought prophecy - as it is written (2 Kings 3:15), "and it came to pass, when the minstrel played, that the hand of the LORD came upon him."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:46: And love is the glory of the soul, that it glorify itself with the glory of the joy with which it rejoices in its God, and cleave to the radiance of the fear of the Name to cling to the splendor of His majesty; and the light of its yearning for its Creator mingles with the love of its longing, the desire of supernal craving, to crown itself with the crown of beauty of pure, clean thoughts - and it moans from the greatness of the gladness of its rejoicing over its beloved, the supernal Beloved, and it binds itself with bonds of affection, and it seeks and inquires after the levels to shine in the light of life. And at the time it is elevated and made great in the knowledge of the holiness of its Creator, and cleaves in its faith to its Maker, then it spreads out in gladness and rejoicing and expands in joy - at that hour it is sanctified with the holiness of the Holy of Holies, and then it becomes beloved and finds favor before the King of kings of kings, and at that time it is established and beautified and adorned with the splendor, pride, might, and glory of love's beauty - and then the Supernal One treasures it, to make its splendor shine, to bring it into the chambers of radiance, and to bind it in the bond of life. May the Merciful One make us among the people of His service who rejoice in Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:47: This chapter I have compiled from Chovot HaLevavot, in the Gate of Trust, and from the book Beit Middot found among us in manuscript, and what I have added to it, according to what the Name has graciously granted me - as the reader will see what is the addition. And it is upon us to entreat the countenance of God, that He guide us on the path of His commandments and His Torah, to be among the lovers of His Name, Amen, and so may it be His will.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:48: With this the chapter and the Gate are concluded:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:1: Before we enter into the explanation of the attributes of repentance, we must explain how many awakenings there are for it - and when a person reads these words from the discourses of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, his heart will be aroused to repent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:2: Because the Holy One, blessed be He, is abundant in kindness, and created the world in His kindness, freely, without any necessity, because His attribute is to do good, and He desired to do good to existing things and that they recognize His greatness - for this is the essential purpose of the creation of the world, "in order that they know Him," as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Bo El Paroh, page 42b) - and the creation of the whole world was created only for the sake of Israel, who are called "the first" [reishit] - and this is "in the beginning [bereishit] God created" - for the sake of Israel, who are called "reishit," as it is said (Jeremiah 2:3), "Israel is holy to the LORD, the first-fruits [reishit] of His increase."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:3: And the Holy One, blessed be He, in His wisdom, saw the need for the creation of souls through the good inclination and the evil inclination, so that they receive good reward according to their deeds and according to judgment - for if He created without the evil inclination, it would be an angel, and for this the angels were already created. And there is another reason as well, explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 23a), that since man was created with the evil inclination, it is impossible that he not sin - for few are those, according to the view of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, who died only because of the serpent's poison, in whom no sin was found (Shabbat 55b) - and for this, repentance preceded the creation of the world, as explained in Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer (chapter 3), that seven things preceded the world, one of them being repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:4: And so they also said in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 69): we have learned, at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world and wished to create man, He took counsel with the Torah. It said before Him: You seek to create this man? He is destined to sin before You, he is destined to anger You; if You do to him according to his deeds, this world cannot stand before You, all the more so that man. He said to them, is it for nothing that I am called "merciful and gracious, slow to anger"? And before the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created repentance. He said to Repentance: I wish to create man in the world, on condition that when they repent to you of their sins, you be ready to forgive their sins and to atone for them; and at every single moment, repentance is ready for people, and when people repent of their sins, this repentance returns to the Holy One, blessed be He, and atones for all, and judgments are subdued and all are sweetened, and the person is purified of his sin. When is a person purified of his sin? At the hour he enters into this repentance properly - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:5: And behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded us concerning the matter of repentance in His holy Torah, through Moses our teacher, peace be upon him (Numbers 5:6), "when a man or woman shall commit any of the sins of man... then they shall confess their sin which they have done, and he shall recompense his guilt with its principal." And it says (Deuteronomy 4:30), "when you are in distress, and all these things have come upon you, in the latter days, if you turn to the LORD your God, and are obedient to His voice - for the LORD your God is a merciful God; He will not fail you, neither destroy you." And in Parashat Atem Nitzavim it says (ibid. 30:1-2), "and it shall come to pass, when all these things have come upon you, the blessing and the curse," and so on, "and you shall call them to mind," and so on, "and shall return to the LORD your God, and shall obey His voice" - and afterward it says (ibid. 30:8), "and you shall return and obey the voice of the LORD" - and it repeats and says, "when you shall return to the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:6: And Ramban, peace be upon him, wrote in his commentary on the Torah (Parashat Nitzavim, page 121), that also the verse "for this commandment" (ibid. 30:11), if it speaks of the Torah, it should have said "all the commandment which I command you this day," and so on. And although this is not really a difficulty, since he explained all these verses as referring to the Torah, which is called "this Torah" (Numbers 19:14) - nevertheless, the Torah has seventy faces, and it is also possible to settle it concerning repentance, since the attribute of "Zot" [This] is also called repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:7: And in my opinion, the verse "for the matter is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it" is settled thus: "in your mouth" - the confession of words that must be confessed; "and in your heart" - the acceptance of repentance in his heart and the abandonment of the sin; "to do it" - if it was theft, that he return the stolen item, and the like.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:8: Further, our holy Torah awakened for us an awakening of repentance in Parashat Mishpatim, in these verses (Exodus 21:7-8), "and if a man sells his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out," and so on, "if she is displeasing in the eyes of her master." And it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, end of page 96b), in these words: the Torah, which gives counsel to the whole world, saw this, and warned the people of the world, saying, see how much the Holy One, blessed be He, has compassion upon you - a good pearl that He had, He sold to you for nothing, that you be enslaved to it in this world. "And if a man sells his daughter" - this is the Holy One, blessed be He; "his daughter" - this is the holy soul; "to be a maidservant" - to be a maidservant, enslaved among you in this world - I beg of you, at the time it comes to depart the world, "she shall not go out" like the going out of slaves, that she not go out soiled, that she not go out defiled with sins; let her go out free, pure and clean, so that her Master rejoice in her and be praised through her, and give her good reward in the dewy freshness of the Garden of Eden, as it says (Isaiah 58:11), "and satisfy your soul with dewy freshness" - certainly, when she goes out clean and pure as is fitting. But "if she is displeasing in the eyes of her master" - soiled with the filth of sins, and did not appear before him properly - woe to that body that has lost that soul forever! For when souls ascend pure and go out clean from this world, each and every soul enters into the King's ledger book, all by their names, and it is said, this is the soul of so-and-so, destined to be for that body that it left - and then it is written, "which he has betrothed to him" [asher lo ye'adah], with a vav [meaning "for him"]. But when it goes out displeasing in the eyes of its master, defiled with sins and with the filth of transgressions, then it is written "lo ye'adah" with an alef [meaning "not"], and that body is lost from it, and it is not made available to it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:9: Except if her Master desires the repentance of the body - then it is written, "then he shall let her be redeemed" [ve-hefdah], as it is said (Job 33:28), "He will redeem his soul from going into the pit." "And he shall let her be redeemed" - this refers to the person whose intent is to redeem it and return in repentance - and in two senses the Holy One, blessed be He, says "and he shall let her be redeemed": through repentance, after he returns in repentance, He redeems it from the path of Gehinnom.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:10: "He shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people" - who is "a foreign people"? The wretched soul, when it leaves the world, and the person went astray from his path with it - it goes to ascend above, into the holy camps, for the holy camps stand on this path of the Garden of Eden, and the foreign camps stand on that path of Gehinnom. If the soul has merit, how many holy camps are prepared to join with it and bring it into the Garden of Eden; if it has no merit, how many foreign camps are prepared on the path of Gehinnom, and these are the camps of the angels of destruction, ready to take vengeance upon it. The verse comes and admonishes: "he shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people" - these are the angels of destruction. "Seeing he has dealt deceitfully with her" - for the soul, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, guards, makes it guarded so that a foreign people not rule over it, within that covering of protection over it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:11: "And if he betroths her to his son" - come and see how much a person must be careful not to deviate from his path in this world - for if a person merits in this world and guards his soul as is fitting, this is a person in whom the Holy One, blessed be He, delights, and He praises him every day among His retinue, and says, see the holy son I have in that world, thus and thus he acts, thus and thus his deeds are arranged. And when this soul, meritorious, clean, and pure, departs this world, the Holy One, blessed be He, illumines it with several lights every day, calling over it, this is the soul of so-and-so, My son - and this is what is written, "and if he betroths her to his son" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:12: This is an awakening for a person along the path of intellect - that since the soul is the daughter of the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Holy One, blessed be He, gave it over to man in this world against her will, as explained there - and behold, a person makes use of the soul for the needs of the body, and its descent to this world was only for the repair of Torah and commandments, as is known. And this is what he said, "a good pearl that He had, He sold to you for nothing, that you be enslaved to it in this world" - at the very least, what the Holy One, blessed be He, asked of us is not to soil His deposit through the filth of transgressions.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:13: And if it becomes soiled, that he redeem it at once from the husks, as it is said, "then he shall let her be redeemed" - and through this a foreign people will not rule over it in Gehinnom. And this is a second awakening for a person - that it is fitting he have compassion on the clean pearl the Creator gave him, that it is not fitting to soil it, requiring it to go to Gehinnom to be refined - this is what they said in Tractate Shabbat (page 152b) on the verse (Ecclesiastes 12:7), "and the spirit shall return to God" - give it back to Him as He gave it to you - and the intent is to exclude the filth of iniquities, but not that he give it back to Him without the adornments of Torah and commandments - for if it returns as it came, what did it gain by coming into the world?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:14: Further, a third awakening: it is fitting that he be aroused to repent when he considers that the Shechinah is exiled because of us, as it is written (Isaiah 50:1), "and for your transgressions your mother was sent away" - and her release from exile depends on our repentance. Why should not each and every one be aroused to repentance, to lighten from her the yoke of exile, and to illumine what he has blemished in her - as we elaborated in the Gate of Fear, how we blemish her and prolong the exile?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:15: And this aspect is explained in the Tikkunim (page 22a), in these words: woe to the people, for the Holy One, blessed be He, is bound with them in exile, and the Shechinah is bound with them - and it is said of her, "a prisoner cannot free himself from prison" - and her redemption, which is repentance, the supernal Mother, depends on their hands, for she has fifty gates of freedom with her, corresponding to the fifty times the Exodus from Egypt is mentioned in the Torah - this is "and he turned this way and that" [vayifen ko va-cho] - through these fifty letters with which they unify her every day, twice, in "Shema Yisrael," in which there are "ko va-cho" letters [numerically 25+25=50]. "And he saw that there was no man" - who arouses her for their sake, and He looks out from the windows, of which it is said (Malachi 1:9), "entreat now the favor of God, that He be gracious to us," to the One of whom it is said (Numbers 12:13), "O God, please heal her now" - for His healing is in His hand, spread out to receive those who repent - "and he saw that there was no man."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:16: And she looks forth through the window and wails, with a broken cry that is wailing, of which it is said (Genesis 8:6), "and Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made" - and this is the Day of Atonement, for Noah's ark is the supernal Mother, and her window is the middle pillar, in which is light, "and Torah is light," and this is the hidden light. "And he turned this way and that" - peering through the crevices, these are the Ten Days of Repentance - "and he saw that there was no man."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:17: And further she looks out from the windows - these are the windows of the synagogue, for Abba and his sons are imprisoned in the synagogue, and she watches over them every day and gives them sustenance. "And he turned this way and that" - to see if there is anyone aroused in repentance to break their prison, this is what is written (Isaiah 49:9), "to say to the prisoners, go forth, to those who are in darkness, show yourselves." "And he turned this way and that, and he saw that there was no man" - rather, "every man turned to his own way," to his affairs, to his own paths; "every one to his gain, from his quarter," to the gain of this world, to inherit this world - and they are not of those of whom it is said (Exodus 18:21), "able men, who fear God, men of truth, hating unjust gain" - rather, "and he saw that there was no man" - but all cry out in their prayers on the Day of Atonement, like dogs, "give, give us sustenance and pardon and atonement, and life - inscribe us for life" - and they are impudent of soul like dogs, who are the nations of the world, worshippers of idols, who cry out to Him and have no shame - for there is none to call them to repentance, so that the Holy One, blessed be He, restore the Shechinah to Himself in the manner He would restore it to them - and they are likened to dogs, of whom it is said (Psalms 106:35), "and they mingled with the nations, and learned their works," and they are the mixed multitude, who do every kindness for their own sake - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:18: Behold, it is explicit how much we should be aroused to repentance out of love for the Shechinah, to raise her from exile - not in order to receive a reward, and not to resemble the mixed multitude or the idol-worshipping nations mentioned in the discourse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:19: And along the lines that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in this discourse, that one who is impudent comes on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur to say "inscribe us for life" and to ask for pardon and atonement without any arousal of repentance - along these lines, every single day too, when we ask in our prayer several requests, which are the thirteen middle blessings, the Holy One, blessed be He, might say, since you come to ask that I do this and that for you, what repentance have you done? And even though we ask, "return us, our Father, to Your Torah," and "forgive us" [that itself is an implicit call to repent first].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:20: And so we find in Vayikra Rabbah, in Parashat Zot Tihyeh Torat HaMetzora (16:4): we find in the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings, that He has no desire for the praise of the wicked. In the Torah, as it is written (Leviticus 13:45), "and he shall cover his upper lip, and shall cry, unclean, unclean." In the Prophets, as it is written (2 Kings 8:5), "and it happened, as he was telling the king how he had restored a dead body to life, that, behold, the woman whose son he had restored to life cried to the king... and Gehazi said, my lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son" - and were they standing behind the door? The Rabbis say, even if they had been at the end of the world, the Holy One, blessed be He, would have removed them and brought them, so that that wicked man [Gehazi] would not tell of the wonders of the Holy One, blessed be He. In the Writings, as it is written (Psalms 50:16), "but to the wicked God says, what right have you to declare My statutes, and to take My covenant in your mouth?" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:21: And therefore one must repent, so that his prayer and his praise not be despised - and even though we say, "return us... forgive us," an awakening from below is necessarily required, as He says (Malachi 3:7), "return to Me, and I will return to you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:22: And through this may be understood their saying, of blessed memory, in Midrash Eichah, on the verse (Lamentations 5:21), "turn us to You, O LORD, and we shall be turned," in these words: the Community of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, it is Yours to "turn us." He said to them: it is yours, as it is said, "return to Me, and I will return to you." They said before Him: Master of the universe, it is Yours, as it is said (Psalms 85:5), "turn us, O God of our salvation" - therefore it is said, "turn us to You, O LORD, and we shall be turned" - to this point. And this means that Israel ask the Holy One, blessed be He, to open for them thoughts of repentance, like a herald who announces that thoughts of repentance are coming, and the Holy One, blessed be He, answers that repentance must be in deed, that they begin it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:23: And along these lines our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Midrash Shir HaShirim (Rabbah 5:3): Rabbi Yosi said, "open for me, my sister, my love" (Song of Songs 5:2) - the Holy One, blessed be He, said, open for Me an opening the size of the eye of a needle, and I will open for you openings through which wagons and carriages can enter. Rabbi Chanina asked Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, what is the meaning of (Psalms 65:6), "the confidence of all the ends of the earth, and of the far-off seas"? He said to him, repentance is likened to the sea: just as the sea is always open, so the gates of repentance are always open - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:24: Further, a fourth awakening: when a person sees the sudden death of the living, as he says (Job 34:20), "in a moment they die," and so on, and he does not know when he will be called to judgment and to reckoning, it is fitting that he arise and hasten to prepare provisions for his journey - for no person is secure in life even for one day, as they said (Avot, chapter 2, mishnah 10), "repent one day before your death," and they said (Shabbat 153a), let him repent today, lest he die tomorrow - and thus all his days are found in repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:25: And a great rebuke is found on this matter in Avot (chapter 1, mishnah 14), in the teaching, "if I am not for myself, who will be for me? And if not now, when?" And the pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz, peace be upon him, explained, in these words, concerning the intent of the mishnah: he taught three great matters that guide a person to the place of his completeness. The first, that just as a person's life depends on the person himself and not on another - for who will eat and who will be concerned, besides him - so it is with the life of the soul: if he is not concerned for his soul, not to let it be destroyed, who will have mercy on it? And therefore "one who has not learned is liable to death" - for he is deserving of death, in that he has subdued his glorious soul beneath the feet of his animal soul, and did not have compassion on it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:26: The second, they have already said it is forbidden to travel with an ignorant person on the road, lest he kill him - and they gave the reason: one who does not care for his own life, all the more so does not care for his fellow's life. And concerning this he said, "if I am not for myself, who is for me?" - and even so, perhaps [I am not sufficient], this is his saying, "and when I am for myself, what am I?" - teaching that he should forever thirst for Torah and never be satisfied with it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:27: The third, that he not lose a moment of his time - for when will this moment come again, the one you are in now, not even one like it? For the one who is first merits to receive blessing - one who goes to distant seas to hunt for prey to bring back, and finds a fitting time for his request - shall he postpone it? If this is so for the life of the mortal body, how much more so for the life of the soul! Or he might say, behold, I am obligated to serve God, blessed be He, all my days, and when shall I complete what I now lack? For it is not fitting to boast of tomorrow, for would that he stand firm on his own and pay what he owes - and so Pharaoh said to Israel (Exodus 5:13), "fulfill your works, your daily task, on its day" - and do not boast of tomorrow, for who has permitted you even that? Are you not obligated to do tomorrow the same as today? If so, when will you fill the deficiency? And I gathered this pleasant explanation from the words of Rabbi Yosef ibn Shoshan, of blessed memory - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:28: And so King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 144:4), "man is like a breath; his days are as a passing shadow." And they said, of blessed memory: Solomon said (Ecclesiastes 6:12), "for who knows what is good for man," and so on - "like which shadow" he did not specify, and David his father explained, "his days are as a passing shadow" - if you say, like the shadow of a wall, there is substance to it; the shadow of a palm tree, there is substance to it - like which shadow, then? Rav Huna said in the name of Rabbi Acha, like the shadow of a bird, which passes and its shadow passes; and Shmuel said, like the shadow of a bee, which has no substance at all - to this point.
